newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Seguin cancels Bonn visit over delay.
newsitem.headline: France's Seguin cancels Bonn visit over delay.

text.p: French National Assembly president Philippe Seguin cancelled a visit to Bonn on Monday because the German Bundestag had not approved plans for a joint parliamentary consultation forum, his office said.

Seguin had been due to sign an agreement with the speaker of the German lower house, Rita Suessmuth, setting up a 40-member "permanent commission" of the French and German parliaments, due to hold its first semi-annual meeting in Paris in June.
But he was told on Friday that the German parliament had deferred approval of the commission's statutes, a move his aides called "totally incomprehensible."

Parliamentary sources in Bonn said factions in both Chancellor Helmet Kohl's Christian Democrats and their Free Democrat partners complained that they had not been adequately consulted during preparations for the commission.
Preparations have been going on for around 18 months and the sources said the parliamentary parties would meet in the next two weeks or so to discuss how to proceed.
Diplomats in Paris also noted that many people in Bonn were reluctant to cooperate with Seguin, who led the French referendum campaign against the Maastricht treaty on European union in 1992.
